atoms.text: Idioms sind Redewendungen im Englischen, die sowohl in der gesprochenen als auch der geschriebenen Sprache genutzt werden.
atoms.sound: <lang xml:lang='en-GB'>Idioms</lang> sind Redewendungen im Englischen, die sowohl in der gesprochenen als auch der geschriebenen Sprache genutzt werden.

atoms.text: Es gibt eine Menge solcher Redewendungen. Hier ist eine Auswahl von häufig genutzten idioms:
atoms.sound: Es gibt eine Menge solcher Redewendungen. Hier ist eine Auswahl von häufig genutzten <lang xml:lang='en-GB'>idioms</lang>.

atoms.text:
ignorance is bliss
etwas nicht zu wissen ist oft besser, weil es Sorgen/Probleme erspart

example.a: Don't ask him about his estranged sister. Sometimes ignorance is bliss.
example.sound: Don't ask him about his estranged sister. Sometimes ignorance is bliss.

example.a: In a nutshell, the holiday was a disaster.
example.sound: In a nutshell, the holiday was a disaster.

atoms.text:
out of the blue
völlig unerwartet; ohne Vorwarnung

example.a: She called me out of the blue after five years of no contact.
example.sound: She called me out of the blue after five years of no contact.

atoms.text:
when it rains, it pours
mehrere Unglücke passieren gleichzeitig oder kurz nacheinander

example.a: First the car broke down, then my phone ran out of battery. When it rains, it pours.
example.sound: First the car broke down, then my phone ran out of battery. When it rains, it pours.

atoms.text:
to judge a book by its cover
vorschnell nach dem äußeren Erscheinungsbild urteilen

example.a: Never judge a book by its cover! This class might actually be interesting.
example.sound: Never judge a book by its cover! This class might actually be interesting.

atoms.text:
to call it a day
aufhören, Feierabend machen

example.a: I'm really tired. Let's call it a day.
example.sound: I'm really tired. Let's call it a day.

atoms.text:
to feel under the weather
sich unwohl oder krank fühlen

example.a: I'm not joining you guys for the run today. I'm feeling a bit under the weather.
example.sound: I'm not joining you guys for the run today. I'm feeling a bit under the weather.

atoms.text:
to add insult to injury
noch eins draufsetzen; eine schlechte Situation noch verschlimmern

example.a: He was late to the wedding, and to add insult to injury, he forgot the rings.
example.sound: He was late to the wedding, and to add insult to injury, he forgot the rings.

atoms.text:
to kill two birds with one stone
mit einer einzigen Handlung werden zwei verschiedene Ziele/Aufgaben gleichzeitig erreicht

example.a: Picking up my parcel on my way  back home kills two birds with one stone.
example.sound: Picking up my parcel on my way  back home kills two birds with one stone.

atoms.text:
to address the elephant in the room
ein offensichtliches, unangenehmes Thema ansprechen

example.a: Enough with the small talk, let's finally address the elephant in the room.
example.sound: Enough with the small talk, let's finally address the elephant in the room.

atoms.text:
to get out of hand
außer Kontrolle geraten

example.a: This party got out of hand rather quickly.
example.sound: This party got out of hand rather quickly.

atoms.text:
to wrap your head around something
etwas begreifen

example.a: I just can't wrap my head around the fact that you're moving to Canada.
example.sound: I just can't wrap my head around the fact that you're moving to Canada.

atoms.text:
to hit the nail on the head
etwas genau treffen; den Kern der Sache erfassen

example.a: Absolutely, you've hit the nail on the head!
example.sound: Absolutely, you've hit the nail on the head

atoms.text:
to be on the fence about something
unentschlossen sein

example.a: I'm still on the fence about whether to move to London.
example.sound: I'm still on the fence about whether to move to London.

atoms.text:
to cross that bridge when you come to it
sich erst mit einem potentiellen Problem beschäftigen, wenn es tatsächlich auftritt

example.a: We might not have bought all the ingredients, but we'll cross that bridge when we come to it.
example.sound: We might not have bought all the ingredients, but we'll cross that bridge when we come to it.
